explanation: In 1969 the opposition took Caetano’s invitation, campaigned under a loosened censorship, and was given nothing at all: 133,000 votes against 980,000 and not one seat, in a system where a third of the vote in a city is worth no representation whatever. The withdrawal of 1973 is the conclusion drawn from that experiment. The CDEs did not stand aside on principle — they had spent 1969 not standing aside — but because they had tested the opening and knew what it was worth.
